chapters.title: Mobile app
intro: This chapter is for agents and customers who use SupportDesk on a phone.
The SupportDesk app has two modes. In agent mode, you work on tickets, alerts and approvals. In customer mode, you follow your own requests and read help articles.
The app keeps working with a weak connection. It shows saved copies of the screens you opened and sends your messages when the connection returns.

sections.title: Get the app
intro: Your administrator tells you how to install the app on your phone.
The app follows your phone's light or dark setting. You can change this on the **Me** tab.

sections.title: Sign in as an agent
sections.intro: Agents sign in with the same details they use on the desk.
prerequisites: You have a SupportDesk agent account and a connection to the internet.
steps: Open the app.
At the top of the sign-in screen, select **Agent**.

steps.caption: The sign-in screen in agent mode.
steps.alt: SupportDesk mobile sign-in screen with the Agent and Customer choice, the Workspace, Work e-mail and Password fields and the Sign in button, numbered

steps: Select **Sign in**.

steps.text: If the app asks for a verification code, enter it in **Code**, and then select **Verify**.
steps.note: The code comes from your authenticator app or by e-mail. Select **Back** to return to the first screen.

sections.result: The **Home** tab opens. The app keeps you signed in on this phone.

sections.title: Sign in as a customer
sections.intro: Customers use the same e-mail as on the support portal. You can sign in with a password or with a code sent by e-mail.
prerequisites: You have access to your support team's portal.
steps: Open the app, and select **Customer**.

steps.text: In **Help center**, enter your portal name, such as `wings`.
steps.note: The portal name is the part of the portal address after `/portal/`.

steps: Enter your **E-mail**.

steps.caption: The sign-in screen in customer mode.
steps.alt: Mobile sign-in screen in customer mode with Help center and E-mail fields, the Password and E-mail me a code choice and the Sign in button, numbered

substeps: With **Password**, enter your **Password**, and then select **Sign in**.
With **E-mail me a code**, select **Send me a code**. Enter the code in **Code from the e-mail**, and then select **Verify code**.

sections.result: The **My tickets** tab opens. The app keeps you signed in on this phone.

blocks.tip: If the code does not arrive, select **Send a new code**.

blocks.note: The app has no single sign-on, no account creation and no password change. Use the web portal for those.

sections.title: The Home tab for agents
sections.intro: **Home** gives you a quick view of your work. Pull the screen down to refresh it.

blocks.caption: The **Home** tab in agent mode.
blocks.alt: Agent Home tab with the availability button, the Mine queue tile, an SLA chip in My next deadlines and the Tickets tab highlighted and numbered

callouts: Your availability. Select it to change it.
**My queues** shows how many tickets wait in each queue. Select a tile to open that list.
**My next deadlines** lists your open tickets with the nearest SLA deadlines. The chip shows the time left, or how long ago the deadline passed.
The tab bar opens **Home**, **Tickets**, **Alerts**, **Approvals** and **Me**. A number on a tab counts your tickets or unread alerts.

blocks.p: If approvals wait for your decision, **Approvals waiting for you** appears below the tiles.

sections.title: Change your availability
sections.intro: Routing only assigns new tickets to you while you are **Online**. Set yourself to **Away** or **Busy** when you step out.
steps: On **Home**, select your availability at the top right.
Choose **Online**, **Away**, **Busy** or **Offline**. Your current choice says **(current)**.
sections.result: A message confirms your new availability, such as **You are Away.**

blocks.tip: You can also change it on the **Me** tab, under **Availability**.

sections.title: Find and act on tickets
sections.intro: The **Tickets** tab lists tickets by queue. You can search, assign tickets to yourself and close them from the list.
steps: Select the **Tickets** tab.
Choose a queue: **Mine**, **Unassigned**, **Overdue**, **At risk**, **Escalated**, **Waiting**, **Watching** or **All open**. Swipe the row of queues to see them all.
To find a ticket, enter its number, subject or customer in **Search number, subject, customer**.

steps.text: To act on a ticket, select the three dots at the end of its row.
steps.caption: The actions for an unassigned ticket.
steps.alt: Tickets list in the Unassigned queue with an action sheet offering Assign to me, Close ticket and Cancel

steps: Choose **Assign to me** or **Close ticket**. Choose **Cancel** to do nothing.
To open a ticket, select it in the list.
sections.result: The ticket opens, or the list shows the change you made.

blocks.caption: The **Tickets** tab with the **Mine** queue.
blocks.alt: Tickets tab with the search box, the Mine queue, the priority and SLA chips of the first ticket and its actions button highlighted and numbered

callouts: Search by number, subject or customer.
The queues. The selected one is underlined.
Each ticket shows its priority, **Escalated** when escalated, and its SLA chip.
The three dots open the ticket's actions.

list: Swipe a ticket to the right for **Assign to me**. Swipe it to the left for **Close**.
A blue dot next to the status means the customer replied.
**Close ticket** asks you to confirm. The customer is not asked to confirm, and you can reopen the ticket later.
When tickets change, **New activity — refresh** appears at the top. Select it to reload the list.
Pull the list down, or select the refresh button, to reload it. Scroll down to load more tickets.

blocks.note: You see **Assign to me** and **Close** only if your role allows them.

sections.title: Work on a ticket
sections.intro: The ticket screen shows the SLA timers and the conversation. You can change the status, priority and assignee from the top of the screen.
steps: Open the ticket from **Tickets**, **Home** or **Alerts**.

steps.text: To change the status, select the status chip, and choose the new status.
steps.caption: The **Change status** list.
steps.alt: Change status action sheet listing Open, Assigned, Waiting on Customer, Waiting on Third Party, Escalated to Engineering, Resolved, Closed and Cancel

steps: To change the priority, select the priority chip, and choose the new priority.

steps.text: To change the assignee, select the person chip, and choose an option.
steps.note: The list offers **Assign to me**, other agents with their availability and load, and **Unassign**.

steps: Select **Customer** to see the contact, the customer, contracts and previous tickets. Select **Conversation** to go back.
sections.result: **Ticket updated** appears, and the timeline shows the change.

blocks.caption: A ticket in agent mode.
blocks.alt: Ticket 1195 with the status, priority and assignee chips, the SLA chips, the Conversation and Customer choice and the reply box highlighted and numbered

callouts: The status, priority and assignee chips. A grey chip means you cannot change it.
The SLA chips show the time left for the first response, the next response and the resolution. **Escalated** shows the escalation level.
**Conversation** shows the messages and events. **Customer** shows who the customer is.
The reply box. See [Reply or add a note](#mobile-reply).

blocks.caption: The **Customer** section of a ticket.
blocks.alt: Customer section with the contact's name, job, e-mail and phone, the customer with its tier and account manager, and ticket statistics

blocks.p: When colleagues open the same ticket, a line under the details says who is viewing or replying.

blocks.note: If someone else changed the ticket first, the app shows the latest version. Make your change again.

sections.title: Reply or add a note
sections.intro: Reply to the customer, or write an internal note for other agents. You can add photos, files and templates.
steps: Open the ticket, and stay on **Conversation**.
Choose **Reply** or **Internal note** above the text box.
Type your message.

steps.text: Optionally, add attachments or a template.
substeps: The camera button takes a photo.
The paper clip button attaches files from your phone.
The page button inserts a reply template.

steps.text: Select **Send**. For a note, select **Add note**.
steps.caption: A reply ready to send, with the camera, file and template buttons.
steps.alt: Mobile reply box with Reply and Internal note, a typed message, camera, attach and template buttons and the Send button

sections.result: **Reply sent.** or **Note added.** appears, and your message joins the conversation.

list: You can attach up to 10 files to a message.
The app saves what you type on the phone. If you leave the ticket, your text is still there when you come back.
Without a connection, the button says **Queue**. See [Work offline](#mobile-offline).

blocks.note: If new messages arrived while you were writing, the app holds your reply. Read the new messages, and then choose **Send anyway**, **Edit** or **Discard**.

sections.title: Read and acknowledge alerts
sections.intro: The **Alerts** tab shows your notifications, such as assignments, mentions and SLA warnings. Critical alerts need an acknowledgement.
steps: Select the **Alerts** tab. The number on the tab counts unread alerts.
Select an alert to open its ticket. The app marks the alert read.
For a critical alert, select **Acknowledge**.
To mark every alert read, select **Mark all read**.
sections.result: **Acknowledged** replaces the button, and the unread count goes down.

blocks.caption: The **Notifications** screen with SLA alerts.
blocks.alt: Notifications screen listing SLA breach and escalation alerts, some with an Acknowledge button, and Mark all read at the top

blocks.note: Some alerts open in the desktop desk only. The app then says **This item opens in the desktop workbench.**

sections.title: Approve or reject a request
sections.intro: Approvers decide on transfer and workflow requests from the **Approvals** tab.
prerequisites: Your role lets you decide approvals.
steps: Select the **Approvals** tab.
On **To decide**, read the request. Select the ticket line to open the ticket.
Select **Approve** or **Reject**.
Enter a note. For a rejection, explain why, because the requester sees your note.
Select **Approve** or **Reject** in the dialog.
sections.result: **Approved.** or **Rejected.** appears, and the request shows who decided.

blocks.p: **Raised by me** lists the approvals you asked for, with their status.

sections.title: The Me tab
sections.intro: **Me** shows who you are signed in as and holds your settings.

blocks.caption: The **Me** tab in agent mode.
blocks.alt: Me tab with the agent's name, Availability, Appearance, Notifications, Unsent messages and the Sign out button

rows: Shows whether push notifications work on this phone. See [Push notifications](#mobile-push).
Lists messages that wait for a connection, with **Retry** and **Discard**.
Signs you out of this mode on this phone.

blocks.warning: Signing out deletes unsent messages from this phone. The app warns you first. Send or discard them before you sign out.

sections.title: Follow your requests
sections.intro: In customer mode, **My tickets** lists your requests. If your support team allows it, you also see your location's or organisation's tickets.
steps: Select the **My tickets** tab.
If you see **Mine**, **Location** and **Organisation**, choose whose tickets to show.
Choose **Open**, **Needs me**, **Closed** or **All**.
To find a request, type in **Search your tickets**.
Select a request to open it.
sections.result: The request opens with its conversation.

blocks.caption: **My tickets** in customer mode.
blocks.alt: My tickets tab with the Mine scope, the Open filter, the search box and the new request button highlighted and numbered

callouts: Whose tickets to show. It appears only if you may see more than your own.
The status filter. **Needs me** lists requests that wait for your reply or confirmation.
The plus button starts a new request.

blocks.p: The **Waiting for your reply** badge marks requests where support asked you something. Another badge asks you to confirm the fix.

sections.title: Reply, confirm, reopen or rate a request
sections.intro: Open a request to reply to support. You can also confirm a fix, reopen a request and rate the support you received.
steps: Open the request from **My tickets**.
To reply, type in **Write a reply…**, add photos or files if needed, and select **Send**.

steps.text: If you see **Did this solve your problem?**, answer it.
substeps: Select **Yes, close it** if the problem is solved.
Select **No, still a problem**, and say what is still not working. Then select **Reopen**.

steps.text: To reopen a closed request, select **Reopen request**. Enter the reason, and then select **Reopen**.
steps.caption: The **Reopen this request?** dialog.
steps.alt: Reopen this request? dialog with a reason typed and the Cancel and Reopen buttons

steps: To rate the support, select from 1 to 5 stars under **How did we do?**. Add a comment if you like, and then select **Send rating**.
sections.result: A message confirms each action, such as **Reply sent.** or **Thank you for your feedback!**

blocks.caption: A closed request that you can rate and reopen.
blocks.alt: Request 1202 with the How did we do? rating card, the Reopen request button and the reply box highlighted and numbered

callouts: Rate the support. **Send rating** appears after you select the stars.
**Reopen request** and the last date you can reopen.
The reply box. Without a connection, the button says **Queue**.

blocks.warning: **Yes, close it** closes the request at once. It does not ask you to confirm.

sections.title: Start a new request
sections.intro: The **New request** form matches the portal's ticket form. It suggests articles that may already answer your question.
steps: Select the **New request** tab, or the plus button on **My tickets**.

steps.text: Enter a **Subject** of at least 5 characters.
steps.caption: The **New request** form with suggested articles.
steps.alt: New request form with a subject, suggested articles, Description and the About your request fields Department, Category, Product, Installation and Priority
steps.note: If a suggested article answers your question, select it to read it.

steps: Describe the problem in **Description**.
Choose the **Department**, **Category**, **Product**, **Installation** and **Priority**.
Fill in any extra fields. You must fill in the fields that have an asterisk.
To attach files, select **Camera** or **Files**.
Select **Submit request**.
sections.result: A message gives the new request number, such as **Request #1206 created — we will be in touch.**

blocks.p: The app saves the form on your phone as you type. Select **Clear form** to start again.

blocks.note: Without a connection, the button says **Save — submit when online**. The app submits the request when the connection returns.

sections.title: Read help articles
sections.intro: The **Help** tab has the same articles as the portal's knowledge base.
steps: Select the **Help** tab.
Choose a category chip, or keep **All** to see **Popular articles** and **Recently updated**.
To search, type in **Search the help center**.
Select an article to read it.
At the end, answer **Was this article helpful?** with **Yes** or **No**.
sections.result: **Thanks for the feedback!** appears. After **No**, you can select **New request**.

blocks.caption: The **Help** tab with categories and popular articles.
blocks.alt: Help tab with a search box, category chips and a list of popular articles

blocks.note: **Yes** and **No** send your answer at once. Search needs a connection, but articles you opened before stay readable offline.

blocks.p: Customer mode does not include the community, the assistant, troubleshooting guides, profile changes or contracts. Use the web portal for those.

sections.title: Work offline
intro: The app keeps a copy of the screens you opened. When the connection drops, you can still read them.
A banner under the title says you are offline. It also says how many messages wait to be sent.

blocks.caption: A ticket while the phone is offline, with a reply ready to queue.
blocks.alt: Ticket screen with the banner You are offline — showing saved data, read-only, grey chips, and a reply with the Queue button

rows: Show the saved copy, with the time it was saved. They refresh when the connection returns.
Saved on the phone as you type.
Wait in a queue. The button says **Queue**. The app sends them, with their attachments, when the connection returns.
Status, priority, assignee, approvals and ratings
Need a connection. Their buttons are grey while you are offline.
Needs a connection. If you were already signed in, the app opens your saved data.

blocks.p: A queued message is never sent twice, even if the app retries. If the team rejects a queued message, for example because the ticket closed, it shows **Not sent**. Choose **Retry**, **Edit** or **Discard**.
If a colleague replied first, a queued agent reply shows **Not sent — new messages arrived**. Read the new messages, and then choose **Send anyway**, **Edit** or **Discard**.

blocks.warning: Signing out deletes unsent messages from this phone. Check **Unsent messages** on the **Me** tab first.

sections.title: Push notifications
intro: The standard app does not send push notifications yet. The **Me** tab shows **Not available in this build**.
While the app is open, updates still arrive live. Agents see new alerts on the **Alerts** tab at once.
Your organisation can build a version of the app with push notifications. Then the **Me** tab has a **Push notifications on this device** switch.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says **You are offline. Signing in needs a connection.**
troubleshooting.cause: The phone has no connection, so the app cannot check your details.
troubleshooting.fix: Connect to Wi-Fi or mobile data, and then sign in again.

troubleshooting.problem: Sign-in says **The details you entered are not correct.**
troubleshooting.cause: The e-mail, password or code is wrong.
troubleshooting.fix: Check your typing. Customers can choose **E-mail me a code** instead of a password.

troubleshooting.problem: Sign-in says **That help center or workspace does not exist.**
troubleshooting.cause: The **Workspace** or **Help center** name is wrong.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the name with your administrator or support team. For customers, it is the part of the portal address after `/portal/`.

troubleshooting.problem: Sign-in says **Your password has expired. Ask an administrator to reset it.**
troubleshooting.cause: Your agent password is too old.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your administrator to reset your password, and then sign in again.

troubleshooting.problem: A message shows **Not sent** on a ticket or on the **Me** tab.
troubleshooting.cause: The team rejected the message, for example because the ticket is now closed.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the reason under the message. Choose **Retry**, **Edit** or **Discard**.

troubleshooting.problem: A file is not attached, and the app says it is larger than the limit.
troubleshooting.cause: The file is too big, or the message already has 10 attachments.
troubleshooting.fix: Attach a smaller file, or send the extra files in another message.

troubleshooting.problem: A screen says **This list has not been saved on this device yet.**
troubleshooting.cause: You are offline and never opened this screen while online.
troubleshooting.fix: Reconnect, and open the screen once. After that, it is available offline.

troubleshooting.problem: A change says **Someone else changed this ticket — showing the latest version. Try again.**
troubleshooting.cause: A colleague changed the ticket while you were looking at it.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the latest version, and make your change again if it is still needed.

faq.q: Can I use agent mode and customer mode on the same phone?
faq.a: Yes. Choose the mode on the sign-in screen. The app keeps a separate sign-in for each mode.

faq.q: Will a reply I queued offline be sent twice?
faq.a: No. Each queued message has its own marker, so a retry never creates a duplicate.

faq.q: Why don't I get push notifications?
faq.a: The standard app does not include push notifications. Keep the app open to get live updates, or ask your organisation about a build with push notifications.

faq.q: What happens to my unsent messages if I sign out?
faq.a: They are deleted from the phone. The app warns you first, so send or discard them before you sign out.

glossary.definition: The mobile app mode for agents. It shows queues, tickets, alerts and approvals.
The mobile app mode for customers. It shows their requests, a new request form and help articles.
The portal name a customer enters in the mobile app, such as `wings`. It is the part of the portal address after `/portal/`.
Replies, notes and new requests that the mobile app holds until it has a connection.
A message written offline in the mobile app. The app sends it when the connection returns.
A message that appears on a phone even when the app is closed. The standard SupportDesk app does not send them yet.
A state of the mobile app while offline. You can read saved screens, but changes wait for a connection.
